subject: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x

messages.author: 33ce433b2edb51fe
messages.subject: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x
parts:
Hi,

The version prior to the 0.9.x series had widths and heights, where
one could conveniently indicate:

facet_grid (pane ~ ., scale='free_y', heights=c(2,1))

Indicating that the 1st facet is 2x larger then the second.

I want to be able to have a vertically facetted graph, with one pane
2x as large as the other. This does not relate to the range of the
data series being rendered in each pane, rather is for purposes of
being able to put more focus visually on one of the facets.

This sort of scaling of facets (or timeseries rendering panes) is very
common in financial applications, where we want our main panel, say,
for price series to occupy a larger vertical space and have 1/2 or
1/3rd's sized panes with indicators below.

Is there some way to get this behavior? Here is a mockup example:

x <- 1:1000
y1 <- cumsum(rnorm(1000))
y2 <- diff(y1) * 1000

data <- rbind (
data.frame (x = x, y=y1, what='price', pane='price'),
data.frame (x = x[-1], y=y2, what='dp', pane='indicators'))

ggplot() +
geom_line (aes(x=x, y=y, colour=what), data=data) +
facet_grid (pane ~ ., scale='free_y', heights=c(2,1)) +
theme_bw()

This ran previously, but now will only run without the heights
parameter. Note that my real usage is more complex that this, where
there are multiple series in a pane and with different geometries.

Thanks in advance.

Jonathan

messages.author: 33ce433b2edb51fe
messages.subject: Re: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x
parts:
Looking into function: facet_panels.grid, I see the folowing code:

  if (facet$space_free$y) {
    ps <- panel$layout$PANEL[panel$layout$COL == 1]
    heights <- vapply(ps, function(i) diff(panel$range[[i]]$y.range), numeric(1))
    panel_heights <- unit(heights, "null")
  } else {
    panel_heights <- rep(unit(1 * aspect_ratio, "null"), nrow)
  }

This is where the facet heights are set (I believe).  Is there a way to override this?   This function is not visible and hence I cannot override short of building an alternative ggplot.   Better would be a way to allow a function or argument to change the panel size behavior.

Can I reasonably go in and modify the grob tree after this has been rendered without too much difficulty?   Adjusting the size before rendering would be preferable, otherwise the axes labels may become too dense or sparse.

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x
parts:
Here is a way you go:

p <- ggplot() +
geom_line (aes(x=x, y=y, colour=what), data=data) +

facet_grid (pane ~ ., scale='free_y') +
theme_bw()

library(grid)
gt <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p))
gt$heights[[3]] <- unit(2, "null")
grid.draw(gt)

In the future version ggplot2 may have an interface for this task.

messages.subject: Re: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x
parts:
Thanks (yes Kohske, was the one who originally provided this), !   Would be nice to find an acceptable way to get this in as a permanent feature.  

I remember that there was some disagreement as to whether this feature should be allowed in the context of a grammar for graphics, in that an artificial scaling does not match 1:1 with the actual range.    On the other hand, by using the default equal-sized facets with scale='free_y' or scale='free_x', we have a disconnect between size and domain / range.

Hence, if we allow what is currently supported, adding in this flexibility is no worse conceptually.

If you are prepared to install from source then substitute this file
(http://dl.dropbox.com/u/2323585/facet-grid-.r) with the one in the
ggplot2 source.

The two functions that has been altered is facet_grid() and
facet_panel.grid()... Ideally it should be possible to apply the
changes using assignInNamespace() (thus avoiding creating another
source) but couldn't get it to work with facet_panel.grid()

(anyone has an idea why? -the output is below:

> assignInNamespace('facet_panels.grid', new_facet_panels.grid, ns='ggplot2')
Error in get(S3[i, 1L], mode = "function", envir = parent.frame()) :
object 'facet_panels' of mode 'function' was not found

but it works fine with facet_grid())

Hope it works for you

best wishes

Thomas

parts: Just so that others know.  Koske's adjustment indicated below does work.   I had forgotten that in grid, need to do a "grid.newpage()", as he pointed out.

On Monday, May 21, 2012 12:04:21 PM UTC-4, jshore wrote:
Thanks for this.  This does adjust the size of the 2 facets, though leaves artifacts.  The axis and facet labels ignore the sizing.  I suspect the best approach is to have a way to alter the original size before this gets rendered.

It does give me some more clues about how to access the underlying structure.   Looks like the best approach, unfortunately, is still to modify the package.

On Monday, May 21, 2012 9:47:52 AM UTC-4, kohske wrote:
Here is a way you go:

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_line (aes(x=x, y=y, colour=what), data=data) +
  facet_grid (pane ~ ., scale='free_y') +
  theme_bw()

library(grid)
gt <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p))
gt$heights[[3]] <- unit(2, "null")
grid.draw(gt)

In the future version ggplot2 may have an interface for this task.

messages.subject: Re: facet_grid heights and widths arguments disappeared in 0.9.x
parts:
gt is gtable including panel, axis, title etc.
You can see it by:

> gt$layout
t l b r clip name
12 1 1 8 7 on layout
1 3 3 3 3 off axis-l
2 5 3 5 3 off axis-l
3 3 4 3 4 on panel
4 5 4 5 4 on panel
5 3 5 3 5 on strip-right
6 5 5 5 5 on strip-right
7 6 4 6 4 off axis-b
8 7 4 7 4 off xlab
9 3 2 5 2 off ylab
10 3 6 5 6 off guide-box
11 2 4 2 4 off title

if you want to customize further, inspect where the panel is.
Now the panel's vertical position is 3 and 5.
So
gt$heights[[3]] <- unit(2, "null")

makes the height of the panel on 3rd row double as that on 5rd row.

kohske

parts:
Hi,

You can define a print method for gtable that does the same thing as
print.ggplot,

print.gtable = function (x, newpage = is.null(vp), vp = NULL, ...)
{
if (newpage)
grid.newpage()
if (is.null(vp)) {
grid.draw(x)
}
else {
if (is.character(vp))
seekViewport(vp)
else pushViewport(vp)
grid.draw(x)
upViewport()
}
invisible(data)
}

HTH,

b.
